subsection.title: Learning Objectives
subsection.p: After completing this section, you should be able to:

list.item: Define and calculate percent.
Convert between percent, decimal, and fractional values.
Calculate the total, percent, or part.
Solve application problems involving percents.

subsection.title: Define and Calculate Percent
subsection.p: The word percent comes from the Latin phrase per centum, which means “by the hundred.” So any percent is a number divided by 100. Changing a percent to a fraction is to write the percent in its fractional form. To write $$n$$% in its fractional form is to write the percent as the fraction $$\frac{n}{100}$$.

note.p: A percent need not be an integer and does not have to be less than 100.

problem.p: Rewrite the following as fractions:

list.item: Using the definition and $$n$$ = 18, 18% in fractional form is $$\frac{18}{100}$$.
Using the definition and $$n$$ = 84, 84% in fractional form is $$\frac{84}{100}$$.
Using the definition and $$n$$ = 38.7, 38.7% in fractional form is $$\frac{38.7}{100}$$.
Using the definition and $$n$$ = 213, 213% in fractional form is $$\frac{213}{100}$$.

subsection.title: Convert Between Percent, Decimal, and Fractional Values
subsection.p: When any calculation with a percent is to be performed, the form of the percent must be changed, either to its fractional form or its decimal form. We can change a percent into decimal form by dividing the percent by 100 and representing the result as a decimal.

note.p: The decimal form of $$n$$% is found by calculating the decimal value of $$n \div 100$$.

problem.p: Convert the following percents to decimal form:

list.item: To convert 17% to its decimal form, divide 17 by 100. This moves the decimal two places to the left, resulting in 0.17. The decimal form of 17% is 0.17.
To convert 7% to its decimal form, divide 7 by 100. This moves the decimal two places to the left, resulting in 0.07. The decimal form of 7% is 0.07.
To convert 18.45% to its decimal form, divide 18.45 by 100. This moves the decimal two places to the left, resulting in 0.1845. The decimal form of 18.45% is 0.1845.

subsection.p: You should notice that, to convert from percent to decimal form, you can simply move the decimal two places to the left without performing the division.

note.p: To convert the number $$x$$ from decimal form to percent, multiply $$x$$ by 100 and place a percent sign, %, after the number, $$(x \times 100)\%$$.

problem.p: Convert each of the following to percent:

list.item: Using the formula and $$x$$ = 0.34, we calculate $$(0.34 \times 100)\%$$, which gives us 34%.
Using the formula and $$x$$ = 4.15, we calculate $$(4.15 \times 100)\%$$, which gives us 415%.
Using the formula and $$x$$ = 0.0391, we calculate $$(0.0391 \times 100)\%$$, which gives us 3.91%.

subsection.p: You should notice that, to convert from decimal form to percent form, you can simply move the decimal two places to the right without performing the multiplication.

subsection.title: Calculate the Total, Percent, or Part
subsection.p: The word “of” is used to indicate multiplication using fractions, as in “one-fourth of 56.” To find “one-fourth of 56” we would multiply 56 by one-fourth. We can think of percents as fractions with a specific denominator—100. So, to calculate “25% of 52,” we multiply 52 by 25%. But, first we need to convert the percent to either fractional form (25/100) or decimal form. Using the decimal form of 25% we have 0.25 × 52, which equals 13.
In this problem, 52 is the total or base, 25 is the percentage, and 13 is the percentage of 52, or the part of 52. This is sometimes referred to as the amount.

note.p: The mathematical formula relating the total (base), the percent in decimal form, and the part (amount) is $$\mathit{part} = \mathit{percent} \times \mathit{total}$$, or, $$\mathit{amount} = \mathit{percent} \times \mathit{base}$$.
In all calculations, the percent is expressed in decimal form.

subsection.p: Knowing any two of the values in our formula allows us to calculate the third value. In the following example, we know the total and the percent, and are asked to find the percentage of the total.

list.item: Determine 70% of 3,500
Determine 156% of 720

The total is= 3,500, and the percent is= 70. The decimal form of 70% is 0.70. To find the part, or percent of the total, substitute those values into the formula and calculate.From this, we say that 70% of 3,500 is 2,450.$$x$$ $$n$$ $$\begin{array}{rcl} \text{part} & = & {{percent} \times {total}} \\ & = & {0.70 \times 3500} \\ & = & 2450 \end{array}$$

The total is= 720, and the percent is= 156. The decimal form of 156% is 1.56. To find the part, or percent of the total, substitute those values into the formula and calculate.From this, we say that 156% of 720 is 1,123.2.$$x$$ $$n$$ $$\begin{array}{rcl} \text{part} & = & {\text{percent} \times \text{total}} \\ & = & {1.56 \times 720} \\ & = & 1,123.2 \end{array}$$

subsection.p: In the previous example, we knew the total and the percent and found the part using our formula. We may instead know the percent and the part, but not the total. We can use our formula again to solve for the total.

list.item: What is the total if 35% of the total is 70?
What is the total if 10% of the total is 4,000?

The percent is 35, which in decimal form is 0.35. We were given that 35% of the total is 70, so the part is 70. We are to find the total. Substituting into the formula, we haveTo find the total, we solve the equation for the total.From this we see that 200 is the total, or, that 35% of 200 is 70.$$\begin{array}{rcl} \text{part} & = & {\text{percent} \times \text{total}} \\ 70 & = & {0.35 \times \text{total}} \end{array}$$ $$\begin{array}{rcl} 70 & = & {0.35 \times \text{total}} \\ \frac{70}{0.35} & = & \frac{0.35 \times \text{total}}{0.35} \\ 200 & = & \frac{0.35 \times \text{total}}{0.35} \\ 200 & = & \text{total} \end{array}$$

The percent is 10, which in decimal form is 0.1. We were given that 10% of the total is 4,000, so the part is 4,000. Substituting into the formula, we haveTo find the total, we solve the equation for the total.From this we see that 40,000 is the total, or that 10% of 40,000 is 4,000.$$\begin{array}{rcl} \text{part} & = & {\text{percent} \times \text{total}} \\ 4,000 & = & {0.1 \times \text{total}} \end{array}$$ $$\begin{array}{rcl} 4,000 & = & {0.1 \times \text{total}} \\ \frac{4,000}{0.1} & = & \frac{0.1 \times \text{total}}{0.1} \\ 40,000 & = & \frac{0.1 \times \text{total}}{0.1} \\ 40,000 & = & \text{total} \end{array}$$

subsection.p: Similarly, the percent can be found if the total and the percent of the total (the part) are known. This will result in the decimal form of the percent, so it must be converted to percent form.

What percent of 228 is 155?

The total is 228, the percent of the total is 155. Substituting into the formula, we haveTo find the percent, we solve the equation for the percent.We see the percent is 0.6798 (rounded to four decimal places). Converting from the decimal form yields 67.98%. We say that 155 is 67.98% of 228.$$\begin{array}{rcl} \text{part} & = & {\text{percent} \times \text{total}} \\ 155 & = & {\text{percent} \times 228} \end{array}$$ $$\begin{array}{rcl} 155 & = & {\text{percent} \times 228} \\ \frac{155}{228} & = & \frac{\text{percent} \times 228}{228} \\ 0.6798 & = & \frac{\text{percent} \times 228}{228} \\ 0.6798 & = & \text{percent} \end{array}$$

subsection.title: Solve Application Problems Involving Percents
subsection.p: Percents are frequently used in finance, research, science experiments, and even casual conversation. Understanding these types of values helps when consuming media or discussing finances, for instance. Effectively working with and interpreting numbers and percents will help you become an informed consumer of this information.

In most cases, working through what is presented requires you to identify that you are indeed working with a question of percents, which two of the three values that are related through percents are known, and which of the three values you need to find.

problem.p: Justine applies to a medium size university outside her hometown and finds out that the retention rate (percent of students who return for their sophomore year) for the 2021 academic year at the university was 84%. During a visit to the registrar’s office, she finds out that 1,350 people had enrolled in academic year 2021. How many students from the academic year 2021 are returning for the 2022 academic year?

solution.p: The percent of students who will return for the 2022 academic year (the retention rate) is 84%. The total number of students who enrolled in the 2021 academic year was 1,350. This means the percent is known and the total is known. From this, we can determine the number of students who will return (percent of the total) for the 2022 academic year using the formula $$\text{part} = \text{percent} \times \text{total}$$. Substituting into the formula and calculating, we find that the number of students that are returning is
So 1,134 students will return for the 2022 academic year.

Percent Error. When performing a scientific experiment that results in quantities of some sort, such as mass in chemistry or momentum in physics, the percent error is often computed. Percent error, %$$E$$, is the percent by which the value obtained in an experiment, the observed value $$O$$, is different than the value that was expected, the expected value $$E$$, in the experiment. The formula is below. $$\% E = \frac{|O - E|}{E}$$ Jim and Kelly are working on a chemistry experiment and expect the result to be 50 grams. However, their result was 48.7 grams. Find Jim and Kelly’s percent error.
